shellcheck:SC2086.title: Unquoted variable expansion (word splitting / globbing)
shellcheck:SC2086.fix: Quote the variable: change `cmd $var` to `cmd "$var"`. Use `"${arr[@]}"` for arrays. If you really want word splitting, add a comment justifying it and a `# shellcheck disable=SC2086` directive on that line.
shellcheck:SC2086.reproduce:
```bash
file="my report.txt"
rm $file        # SC2086 — splits into two args: rm 'my' 'report.txt'
# Broken output:  rm: cannot remove 'my': No such file or directory
#                rm: cannot remove 'report.txt': No such file or directory
# Fixed:
rm "$file"     # treats 'my report.txt' as one path
```

shellcheck:SC2046.title: Unquoted command substitution (word splitting)
shellcheck:SC2046.fix: Wrap the substitution in double quotes: `"$(cmd)"`. If you intentionally want a list of args, switch to an array: `mapfile -t items < <(cmd)`.
shellcheck:SC2046.reproduce:
```bash
echo $(printf 'a b\nc')   # SC2046 — splits into 3 words
# Broken output: a b c   (newline collapsed, words split)
# Fixed:
echo "$(printf 'a b\nc')"
# Output: a b\nc          (preserved)
```

shellcheck:SC2155.title: Declare and assign separately to avoid masking return values
shellcheck:SC2155.fix: Split the declaration from the assignment so the exit code of the command substitution isn't swallowed by `local`/`export`/`readonly`.
shellcheck:SC2155.reproduce:
```bash
local x=$(false)         # SC2155 — exit code is 0 (from `local`), not 1 (from `false`)
echo $?                  # 0  ← bug, masked failure
# Fixed:
local x
x=$(false)
echo $?                  # 1  ← correct
```

njsscan:eval_nodejs.title: Use of eval() — code injection risk
njsscan:eval_nodejs.fix: Replace `eval(input)` with a parser/evaluator scoped to your data shape. For JSON use `JSON.parse(input)`. For arithmetic use a dedicated lib (e.g. `mathjs.evaluate`). Never feed user input into `eval`, `new Function`, `setTimeout(string, ...)`, or `vm.runInThisContext`.

semgrep:javascript.lang.security.audit.e.title: eval() used on attacker-influenced input
semgrep:javascript.lang.security.audit.e.fix: Same as njsscan:eval_nodejs — never `eval` untrusted input. Use a typed parser (`JSON.parse`, `zod.parse`, a small grammar) or a sandboxed evaluator (`vm2` is deprecated; prefer isolated-vm or QuickJS-WASM).

retire:jquery.title: Outdated jQuery with known XSS in $.html()/$.append()
retire:jquery.fix: Upgrade jQuery to ≥ 3.5.0 (fixes CVE-2020-11022/11023). If the version is pinned by a transitive dep, override it: in `package.json` add `"pnpm": { "overrides": { "jquery": "^3.5.1" } }` then `pnpm install`.
retire:jquery.reproduce: ```html ```

lockfile-lint:lockfile-integrity.title: Lockfile points to non-https or non-allowlisted hosts
lockfile-lint:lockfile-integrity.fix: Inspect the offending entries in `pnpm-lock.yaml` (search for `http://` or unexpected hostnames). Re-resolve by deleting the suspicious lines and running `pnpm install`. If the entry is from a private registry, add it to `--allowed-hosts`. Commit the regenerated lockfile.
lockfile-lint:lockfile-integrity.reproduce:
```yaml
# pnpm-lock.yaml fragment that lockfile-lint flags:
'/some-pkg@1.0.0':
  resolution: { tarball: 'http://evil.example.com/some-pkg-1.0.0.tgz' }   # http, not https; unknown host
# Broken output: any teammate running `pnpm install` fetches from evil.example.com — full RCE during install.
# Fixed entry resolves from `https://registry.npmjs.org/...` only.
```

madge:circular-dependency.title: Circular import between modules
madge:circular-dependency.fix: Break the cycle by extracting the shared symbol into a third module that both sides import. Or invert the dependency: have the lower-level module accept the dependency via a function parameter / DI container instead of importing the higher-level one.

trivy:secret.title: Hard-coded secret in source tree
trivy:secret.fix: Rotate the secret immediately at the provider, then move it into an environment variable / secret manager. Replace the literal in code with `process.env.MY_SECRET`. Add the file to `.gitignore` and rewrite history with `git filter-repo` if it ever landed on a shared branch.

expo-doctor:generic.title: expo-doctor reported environment / config issues
expo-doctor:generic.fix: Run `pnpm --filter @workspace/lexi-mobile exec expo-doctor` locally to see the full list. Common fixes: `pnpm exec expo install --check` to align native dep versions to the current Expo SDK, then commit the updated `package.json` / lockfile.
expo-doctor:generic.reproduce:
```text
# Symptom that expo-doctor flags:
#   ✖ Validating dependency versions for installed Expo SDK
#     Expected react-native@0.74.5; found react-native@0.73.6
# Broken output at runtime: app crashes on launch with native-module mismatch errors
# (e.g. 'TurboModuleRegistry.getEnforcing(...): "..." could not be found').
# Fixed by `expo install --check` which pins react-native to the SDK-matched version.
```
